item.title: Crews battling prescribed burn that 'got out of control' in Burnet County
item.description: Fire crews in Burnet County are battling a 75-acre prescribed burn that "got out of control" Monday, the Marble Falls Area Volunteer Fire Department Said.

item.title: Texas family raffling off 100 acres of mineral rights for $4
item.description: A Texas family is raffling 100 acres of mineral rights after years of low‑ball offers, giving one winner a chance to claim a century‑old Texas legacy.

item.title: Longhorns sophomore Justice Carlton is 'Rollin' in Dough'
item.description: Being a Division I athlete is demanding, and like the average person working a 9-to-5, student-athletes need an outlet. Sophomore forward Justice Carlton has turned her love for baking into her personal business adventure, "J's Rollin In Dough."

item.title: A Texan scored her 1st Olympic goal as US routs Switzerland 5-0
item.description: Coppell's Hannah Bilka scored her first Olympic goal in a 5-0 rout of Switzerland on Monday at Milano Santaguilia Hockey Arena, and said the moment was "super special."

item.title: Words exchanged, car kicked before man accused of assaulting girl at Buda student walk-out
item.description: Police made and arrest and released new details after a fight broke out between a man and a group of juveniles during a student-led walkout protest in Buda. The students were protesting Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) on Monday, Feb 2 when an argument escalated to physical violence, according to Buda PD.

item.title: Two storms this week: One small and one bigger
item.description: Our second rain chance is much more promising with rain arriving late Friday and continuing through Saturday afternoon. -- Nick Bannin

item.title: Democrats issue ICE reform demands ahead of DHS funding fight
item.description: If Congress does not reach a deal by Friday, funding for the U.S. Department of Homeland Security will expire, and House Democrats are pushing for immigration enforcement reforms in exchange for their support.

item.title: 30 drownings in a decade: Lady Bird Lake serial killer myth continues to haunt Austin
item.description: Despite city safety initiatives aimed at preventing more tragedies, bodies continued surfacing – along with suspicions of a serial killer preying on intoxicated victims venturing too close to the lake’s edge.

item.title: APD investigating after man accused of abusing, causing 'unjustified pain' to dog
item.description: The Austin Police Department is investigating an animal cruelty case after a man was accused of abusing a dog on an apartment balcony.

item.title: Downtown Austin lake deaths echo other cities: men in 30s, alcohol
item.description: For years, police in Texas’ capital city have maintained there is no serial killer drowning intoxicated victims in Lady Bird Lake. Despite suspicion surrounding such a predator, Sgt. Nathan Sexton with the local homicide unit told KXAN that Austin is no different from other places when it comes to drownings.
